mmaths-2023-lightning-01.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-01.body:
Bob should guess $1001$. Then he is strictly closer for every number $k\ge1001$ (the midpoint $1000.5$ is not an integer, so there are no ties), i.e. for $2023-1000=1023$ numbers. Guessing $999$ would win only $999$ numbers, and any other guess is worse. Probability $\frac{1023}{2023}$.

**Answer: 1023/2023**

mmaths-2023-lightning-03.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-03.body:
Eggs allow $\frac{18}{6}=3$ batches, flour allows $\frac{24}{12}=2$ batches. The limiting ingredient is flour: $2\cdot24=48$ servings.

**Answer: 48**

mmaths-2023-lightning-04.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-04.body:
The first charger delivers $3$ phone batteries per hour, so the faster one delivers $6$ phone batteries per hour. It also delivers $2$ laptop batteries per $1.5$ hours, i.e. $\frac43$ laptop batteries per hour. So $\frac43$ laptop $=6$ phone, a laptop battery is $4.5$ phone batteries: $350\%$ bigger.

**Answer: 350**

mmaths-2023-lightning-05.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-05.body:
The table is a regular hexagon with apothem $4\sqrt3\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}2=6$. The coin lies entirely on the table iff its center is at distance at least $3$ from every side, i.e. in the concentric similar hexagon of apothem $6-3=3$. The linear ratio is $\frac12$, so the area ratio is $\frac14$.

**Answer: 1/4**

mmaths-2023-lightning-06.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-06.body:
If $x$ rooms hold $6$, the capacity is $6x+8(12-x)=96-2x=74$, so $x=11$.

**Answer: 11**

mmaths-2023-lightning-07.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-07.body:
The number studying at least one subject is between $51\%$ (economics is a subset of CS) and $100\%$ (no overlap, $49+51=100$). So 'neither' ranges from $0\%$ to $49\%$, a difference of $49$ percentage points.

**Answer: 49**

mmaths-2023-lightning-08.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-08.body:
Take a quarter-circle (a $90^\circ$ sector) of radius $r$. Put its two straight edges' far ends $P,Q$ on the unit circle with $PQ$ a diameter; the apex $V$ then lies on the unit circle as well (right angle subtends a diameter) and $PQ=r\sqrt2=2$ gives $r=\sqrt2$. The arc of radius $\sqrt2$ centered at $V$ stays inside the unit circle (its points are at distance $\sqrt{3-2\sqrt2\cos\varphi}\le1$ from the center for $|\varphi|\le45^\circ$). This is the biggest possible, since the two arc endpoints lie in the unit disk, so $r\sqrt2\le2$. Area $=\frac14\pi(\sqrt2)^2=\frac\pi2$.

**Answer: pi/2**

mmaths-2023-lightning-09.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-09.body:
Count the maximum for each pair: square-triangle: each of the $3$ triangle sides meets the (convex) square boundary in at most $2$ points, so $6$; square-circle: $2$ per side, $8$; triangle-circle: $6$; line-square: $2$; line-triangle: $2$; line-circle: $2$. Total $6+8+6+2+2+2=26$, and all can occur simultaneously.

**Answer: 26**

mmaths-2023-lightning-10.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-10.body:
Each flip changes her money by $\pm1$. After $2023$ (an odd number of) flips her net change is odd, hence never $0$. The probability is $0\%$.

**Answer: 0**

mmaths-2023-lightning-11.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-11.body:
Choosing $3$ non-adjacent positions out of $9$ is equivalent (shrink each gap by one) to choosing $3$ positions out of $9-2=7$: $\binom73=35$.

**Answer: 35**

mmaths-2023-lightning-12.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-12.body:
The pentagon turns at $36^\circ$ per minute and the triangle at $60^\circ$ per minute. The labelled vertices are back in their starting positions only after a full turn: the pentagon after $\frac{360}{36}=10$ minutes, the triangle after $\frac{360}{60}=6$ minutes. Both after $\operatorname{lcm}(10,6)=30$ minutes.

**Answer: 30**

mmaths-2023-lightning-13.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-13.body:
Choose the number of tens $t=0,1,2,3$. The rest ($36-10t$) is paid with fives and ones: the number of fives can be $0,1,\dots,\lfloor\frac{36-10t}5\rfloor$: $8,6,4,2$ choices. Total $8+6+4+2=20$.

**Answer: 20**

mmaths-2023-lightning-15.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-15.body:
Each draw either swaps a red ball for a green one (total unchanged) or adds one green ball. Exactly $20$ of the $460$ draws were red, so $440$ were green draws, each adding one ball. The bag then has $40+440=480$ balls, all green.

**Answer: 480**

mmaths-2023-lightning-16.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-16.body:
Numbers one more than a multiple of $9$ have digit sum $\equiv1\pmod9$. Two-digit such numbers: $10,19,28,37,46,55,64,73,82,91$; the primes are $19,37,73$, all with $A+B=10$.

**Answer: 10**

mmaths-2023-lightning-18.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-18.body:
One more than a multiple of $7$ in $1..64$: $1,8,\dots,64$, that is $10$ numbers. One more than a multiple of $9$: $1,10,\dots,64$, that is $8$ numbers. Both means $\equiv1\pmod{63}$: $1$ and $64$, $2$ numbers. Exactly one: $(10-2)+(8-2)=14$. Probability $\frac{14}{64}=\frac7{32}$.

**Answer: 7/32**

mmaths-2023-lightning-19.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-19.body:
After $k$ guests, $2^{-k}$ of the pie remains. We need $2^{-k}<0.001$, i.e. $2^k>1000$. Since $2^9=512<1000<1024=2^{10}$, the minimum is $k=10$.

**Answer: 10**

mmaths-2023-lightning-20.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-20.body:
$\frac{\sqrt3}4s^2=64\sqrt3$ gives $s=16$, perimeter $48$. The square has side $12$ and area $144$.

**Answer: 144**

mmaths-2023-lightning-22.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-22.body:
The largest possible distance between two points of the cube is the space diagonal $2\sqrt3\approx3.46<4$, so the distance is always less than $4$: probability $1$.

**Answer: 1**

mmaths-2023-lightning-23.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-23.body:
With cube side $s$ the prism is $s\times s\times2s$ with surface area $2s^2+4\cdot2s^2=10s^2=250$, so $s=5$. Volume $2s^3=250$.

**Answer: 250**

mmaths-2023-lightning-24.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-24.body:
$AE$ and $BF$ are diameters of the circumcircle, so $O$ is the center. Adjacent vertices subtend a central angle of $\frac{360^\circ}{8}=45^\circ$.

**Answer: 45**

mmaths-2023-lightning-26.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-26.body:
While on and plugged in, the battery gains $\frac12\%$ per minute from charging and loses $\frac15\%$ per minute to consumption: net $\frac12-\frac15=\frac3{10}\%$ per minute. It must gain $50\%$, taking $\frac{50}{3/10}=\frac{500}{3}=166\frac23$ minutes.

**Answer: 500/3**

mmaths-2023-lightning-27.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-27.body:
$180-50=130$ like at least one subject. By inclusion-exclusion, $110+100-\text{both}=130$, so both $=80$.

**Answer: 80**

mmaths-2023-lightning-28.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-28.body:
The tank needs $0.8\cdot60=48$ gallons, which cost $48\cdot1.50=72$ dollars.

**Answer: 72**

mmaths-2023-lightning-29.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-29.body:
This is Nim with two piles; the player to move loses exactly when the piles are equal. Blice must leave equal piles, so she takes $9-4=5$ coins from the larger pile. Afterwards she copies every move of Aob on the other pile and takes the last coin.

**Answer: 5**

mmaths-2023-lightning-30.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-30.body:
$C=B+2$ is a digit that is a perfect square: $0,1,4,9$. $C=9$ gives $B=7$ (prime), $A=8$ (even): $879$. $C=4$ gives $B=2$, $A=3$ which is odd, rejected. So the number is $879$.

**Answer: 879**

mmaths-2023-lightning-31.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-31.body:
By the Law of Cosines in $\triangle ABC$: $AC^2=49+50-2\cdot7\cdot5\sqrt2\cos135^\circ=99+70=169$, so $AC=13$. The other diagonal $BD$ is twice the altitude from $B$ in $\triangle ABC$: the area is $\frac12\cdot7\cdot5\sqrt2\sin135^\circ=\frac{35}2$, the altitude is $\frac{35}{13}$, so $BD=\frac{70}{13}<13$. The longer diagonal is $13$.

**Answer: 13**

mmaths-2023-lightning-32.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-32.body:
$\sum k^3=\left(\frac{2023\cdot2024}2\right)^2=2047276^2$. $2047276$ is even and has digit sum $28\equiv1\pmod3$, so $2047276\equiv4\pmod6$ and its square $\equiv16\equiv4\pmod6$.

**Answer: 4**

mmaths-2023-lightning-33.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-33.body:
The original surface area is $2\pi\cdot25+2\pi\cdot5\cdot15=50\pi+150\pi=200\pi$. The cut exposes two new circular faces of area $25\pi$ each: $+50\pi$. The increase is $\frac{50}{200}=25\%$.

**Answer: 25**

mmaths-2023-lightning-35.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-35.body:
The area outside the square is $280-16=264$ square meters, so the density there is $\frac{1320}{264}=5$ per square meter. Inside the square it is $15$ per square meter: $15\cdot16=240$.

**Answer: 240**

mmaths-2023-lightning-36.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-36.body:
The minute hand gains $5.5^\circ$ per minute on the hour hand, and at $9{:}00$ it is $270^\circ$ behind, so it first passes after $\frac{270}{5.5}=49\frac1{11}$ minutes (at about $9{:}49$). After that it passes every $\frac{360}{5.5}=65\frac5{11}$ minutes: at about $10{:}54$, $12{:}00$, and $1{:}05\frac5{11}$. The fourth time is $1{:}05$ PM.

**Answer: 1:05 PM**

mmaths-2023-lightning-37.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-37.body:
A set of lengths with no triangle must grow like Fibonacci: sorted $a_1<a_2<\dots$ with $a_{k+2}\ge a_k+a_{k+1}$. Starting from $1,2$: $1,2,3,5,8$ is the longest such set within $1..9$ (the next term would be $13>9$), with $5$ sticks. So $5$ sticks can fail, but any $6$ sticks must contain a triangle.

**Answer: 6**

mmaths-2023-lightning-38.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-38.body:
Rain tomorrow only: $0.3\cdot(1-0.4)=0.18$. Rain the day after only: $0.7\cdot0.2=0.14$. Sum $0.32=32\%$.

**Answer: 32**

mmaths-2023-lightning-41.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-41.body:
They approach each other at $12$ m/s and must cover a total of $360$ m between meetings, so they meet every $30$ seconds. In $600$ seconds that is $\frac{600}{30}=20$ meetings (including the one at exactly $10$ minutes).

**Answer: 20**

mmaths-2023-lightning-43.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-43.body:
Worst case: Sam has no two disjoint matching pairs yet with as many socks as possible: all $3$ socks of one color (only one disjoint pair) plus $1$ sock of each of the other $4$ colors, $7$ socks. The remaining socks are all of the four colors that have one sock so far, so the $8$th sock completes a second pair, disjoint from the first. Hence $8$ socks are needed.

**Answer: 8**

mmaths-2023-lightning-44.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-44.body:
Exterior angles are $3^\circ$ and $5^\circ$, so $n=\frac{360}3=120$ and $m=\frac{360}5=72$. $n-m=48$.

**Answer: 48**

mmaths-2023-lightning-46.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-46.body:
Surface sub-cubes = total minus interior: size $4$: $64-8=56$; size $5$: $125-27=98$. $56$ cubes take $28$ s, so $98$ cubes take $49$ s.

**Answer: 49**

mmaths-2023-lightning-47.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-47.body:
$50\to40\to32$ (sale price), then $32\cdot1.4=44.8$. The difference from $50$ is $5.20$ dollars.

**Answer: 5.2**

mmaths-2023-lightning-48.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-48.body:
$\angle A=180^\circ-23^\circ-38^\circ=119^\circ$. Let $\angle BAD=x$; then $\angle DAE=2x$, $\angle EAC=4x$ and $7x=119^\circ$, so $x=17^\circ$ and $\angle EAC=68^\circ$.

**Answer: 68**

mmaths-2023-lightning-49.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-49.body:
Adjacent corners may not be labelled $1$ and $3$. Choose the labels of opposite corners $A$ and $C$ first; then $B$ and $D$ are chosen independently, each from the labels compatible with both $A$ and $C$, i.e. from $N(A)\cap N(C)$ where $N(1)=\{1,2\}$, $N(2)=\{1,2,3\}$, $N(3)=\{2,3\}$. Sizes $|N(A)\cap N(C)|$: $(1,1)$: $2$; $(2,2)$: $3$; $(3,3)$: $2$; $(1,2),(2,1),(2,3),(3,2)$: $2$ each; $(1,3),(3,1)$: $1$ each. The number of ways is $\sum_{A,C}|N(A)\cap N(C)|^2=4+9+4+4\cdot4+2\cdot1=35$.

**Answer: 35**

mmaths-2023-lightning-50.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-50.body:
The diagonals are perpendicular bisectors. A half-diagonal of $12$ and the side $20$ give the other half-diagonal $\sqrt{400-144}=16$, so the other diagonal is $32$. Area $=\frac{24\cdot32}{2}=384$.

**Answer: 384**

mmaths-2023-lightning-51.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-51.body:
Let $d,w$ be the calories: $2d+5w=194$, $4d+w=145$. Doubling the first: $4d+10w=388$; subtracting the second gives $9w=243$, so $w=27$ (and $d=29.5$).

**Answer: 27**

mmaths-2023-lightning-52.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-52.body:
Cone: $\frac13\pi(6r)^2\cdot\frac h2=6\pi r^2h$. Cylinder: $\pi r^2h$. Ratio $6$.

**Answer: 6**

mmaths-2023-lightning-53.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-53.body:
The center is at distance $\frac12\sqrt{2^2+4^2+6^2}=\frac12\sqrt{56}=\sqrt{14}$ from each vertex.

**Answer: sqrt(14)**

mmaths-2023-lightning-54.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-54.body:
Four cases hold at most $28<32$. Five cases: $7a+5b+3c=32$ with $a+b+c=5$ gives $4a+2b=17$, impossible (odd). Six cases work: $7+7+7+5+3+3=32$.

**Answer: 6**

mmaths-2023-lightning-55.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-55.body:
The car takes $\frac{1}{60}$ h $=60$ s and the train $\frac1{40}$ h $=90$ s. The difference is $30$ seconds.

**Answer: 30**

mmaths-2023-lightning-57.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-57.body:
From the inside: $2+1=3$; $3+\frac13=\frac{10}3$; $4+\frac3{10}=\frac{43}{10}$; the reciprocal is $\frac{10}{43}$.

**Answer: 10/43**

mmaths-2023-lightning-58.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-58.body:
They all sound together every $\operatorname{lcm}(2,4,6,8)=24$ minutes, so at $8{:}24$.

**Answer: 8:24**

mmaths-2023-lightning-60.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-60.body:
The diagonal from $(0,0)$ to $(9,0)$ lies on the $x$-axis. By the shoelace formula for the quadrilateral $(0,0),(3,a),(9,0),(6,b)$ the area is $\frac12|{-9a}+9b|=\frac92|a-b|=72$, so $|a-b|=16$. With $(3,a)$ above the axis and $(6,b)$ below, $a-b=16$.

**Answer: 16**

mmaths-2023-lightning-61.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-61.body:
The terms from $-50$ to $50$ cancel in pairs, leaving $51+52+53=156$.

**Answer: 156**

mmaths-2023-lightning-62.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-62.body:
A drawing order is a sequence of $8$ draws containing $4$ reds and $4$ blues: $\binom84=70$.

**Answer: 70**

mmaths-2023-lightning-63.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-63.body:
A number with $6$ divisors is $p^5$ or $p^2q$. With primes in $\{2,3,5\}$ the candidates are $2^5=32$, $3^5=243$, $5^5=3125$, and $p^2q$ with value at most $5^2\cdot3=75$ or $3^2\cdot5=45$, etc. The largest is $5^5=3125$.

**Answer: 3125**

mmaths-2023-lightning-64.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-64.body:
Equal arc lengths: $74r_1=111r_2$, so $\frac{r_1}{r_2}=\frac{111}{74}=\frac32$. The areas have ratio $\left(\frac32\right)^2=\frac94$.

**Answer: 9/4**

mmaths-2023-lightning-65.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-65.body:
The primes are $101,103,107,109$ (the other numbers are divisible by $2,3,5,7$ or $11$). Sum $=420$.

**Answer: 420**

mmaths-2023-lightning-66.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-66.body:
The sequence starts $3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23,31,\dots$. For $n\ge2$ the terms alternate between residues $1$ and $5$ mod $6$ ($p_2=5$, $p_3\equiv1$, $p_4\equiv5,\dots$), so $p_n+p_{n+1}\equiv0\pmod 6$ and is at least $12$; a multiple of $6$ is divisible by two different primes, so not a prime power. Only $p_1+p_2=3+5=8=2^3$ qualifies. The sum of all such values is $8$.

**Answer: 8**

mmaths-2023-lightning-67.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-67.body:
$216=2^3\cdot3^3$. Every number $2^a3^b$ with $0\le a,b\le3$ lies on some path from $1$ to $216$, and nothing else does. The sum is $(1+2+4+8)(1+3+9+27)=15\cdot40=600$.

**Answer: 600**

mmaths-2023-lightning-68.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-68.body:
If all three were odd the sum would be odd, so $p=2$ and $q+r=46$. Prime pairs: $(3,43),(5,41),(17,29)$ (and $23+23$ is not distinct). The smallest difference is $29-17=12$.

**Answer: 12**

mmaths-2023-lightning-69.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-69.body:
Let each youngest sibling get $x$. Then the second oldest gets $2x$ and the oldest $4x$. $x+x+2x+4x=8x=128$, so $x=16$ and the oldest gets $64$.

**Answer: 64**

mmaths-2023-lightning-70.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-70.body:
Each vertex appears in two midpoints with weight $\frac12$ each, so the sum of the midpoint coordinates equals the sum of the vertex coordinates: $0+0+3+7+8+2=20$.

**Answer: 20**

mmaths-2023-lightning-72.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-72.body:
$12^3=2^6\cdot3^3$ and $18^3=2^3\cdot3^6$. Common divisors are the divisors of $\gcd=2^3\cdot3^3$, which has $(3+1)(3+1)=16$ divisors.

**Answer: 16**

mmaths-2023-lightning-73.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-73.body:
The ammonia stays $5$ mL, and we need $5=0.02\cdot\text{total}$, so the total is $250$ mL. Add $250-100=150$ mL of water.

**Answer: 150**

mmaths-2023-lightning-75.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-75.body:
It holds $6$ gallons, so it can go $6\cdot35=210$ miles.

**Answer: 210**

mmaths-2023-lightning-76.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-76.body:
We need $\gcd(k,6)=1$, i.e. $k$ is divisible by neither $2$ nor $3$. By inclusion-exclusion: $100-50-33+16=33$.

**Answer: 33**

mmaths-2023-lightning-78.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-78.body:
$\sqrt{x^6+2x^3+1}=|x^3+1|$. If $x^3+1\ge0$ the left side is $1$, not greater than $1$. If $x^3<-1$ it is $-x^3-1-x^3=-2x^3-1>1\iff x^3<-1$. So the inequality holds exactly for $x<-1$, and the largest integer is $-2$.

**Answer: -2**

mmaths-2023-lightning-79.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-79.body:
All terms are positive, so $0<a_i<\frac1i$ for $i\ge2$. By the squeeze theorem $a_n\to0$.

**Answer: 0**

mmaths-2023-lightning-80.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-80.body:
Write $z=x-i$; then $z^6=\frac{64}{27}$, so $z=r\,e^{ik\pi/3}$ with $r=\left(\frac{64}{27}\right)^{1/6}=\frac{2}{\sqrt3}$. A real root $x$ requires $\operatorname{Im}z=-1$, i.e. $r\sin\frac{k\pi}3=-1$, $\sin\frac{k\pi}3=-\frac{\sqrt3}2$: $k=4$ or $k=5$ (angles $240^\circ$, $300^\circ$). Two real roots, $x=\mp\frac1{\sqrt3}$.

**Answer: 2**

mmaths-2023-lightning-81.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-81.body:
A number and its digit sum are congruent mod $9$. $2024\equiv8\equiv-1\pmod9$, so $2024^{2023}\equiv(-1)^{2023}=-1\equiv8$.

**Answer: 8**

mmaths-2023-lightning-82.title: Solution
mmaths-2023-lightning-82.body:
Any two distinct vertices need a path of length at least $1$, so the diameter is at least $1$. The complete graph $K_{20}$ is connected and has diameter exactly $1$.

**Answer: 1**
